mainTopic: חרוסת and חמץ; the ban on boiling the פסח, and what counts as נא, raw, and צלי אש
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion from the previous amud about flour mixed into חרוסת or mustard. רב כהנא holds that only the mustard case is disputed, and with חרוסת everyone agrees it must be burned. רב הונא disagrees with him. רב אשי tries to support רב כהנא from שמואל's ruling about vinegar, but the גמרא rejects that proof. Next, the גמרא turns to the משנה's rule against boiling the פסח. The רבנן learn that every liquid is forbidden through a קל וחומר, while רבי learns it from the words ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״. The two sources lead to a practical difference about צלי קדר, meat cooked in a pot in its own juices. The גמרא then explains why boiling after roasting still makes one liable: רב כהנא says the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, and עולא says it is a special rule from the פסוק. Two more ברייתות teach that charred meat and raw meat are not included in the לאו, although raw meat is still forbidden by the command of צלי אש. רב חסדא rules that boiling the פסח in the hot springs of טבריא breaks only the command of צלי אש. Finally, רבא begins a ruling about eating the פסח half-roasted, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Was the ruling about חרוסת or about mustard?
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks רב הונא בריה דרב יהודה which case his ruling referred to: חרוסת or חרדל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did the Master say this about חרוסת, or did the Master say it about mustard?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק asks for clarification about the ruling he just heard, that the הלכה follows the חכמים. He wants to know exactly which mixture it referred to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two cases together: flour put into חרוסת and flour put into mustard. The questioner suspects the two cases might not have the same law. So he asks which case the ruling ('the הלכה follows the חכמים') was actually about.

keyTerms.meaning: A dip made of fruit, nuts and vinegar, used at the סדר
Mustard
'Is the Master saying' – a respectful way of asking a teacher what he meant

phrases.english: Was it about charoset that the Master said it,
phrases.notes: The little א at the start stands for על, so it means 'about charoset.'

phrases.english: or was it about mustard that the Master said it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַחֲרוֹסֶת קָאָמַר מָר, אוֹ אַחַרְדָּל קָאָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a clarification of the ruling given on the previous amud (that the הלכה follows the חכמים).
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which of the two cases in the ברייתא (חרוסת or חרדל) the ruling 'הלכה כחכמים' was referring to.

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers the question with a question: why does it matter which case was meant?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What practical difference does it make?
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא responds by asking why the distinction matters. This sets up the next step, where the questioner explains his reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From רב הונא's point of view, the ברייתא puts חרוסת and mustard side by side, so the same law should apply to both. His counter-question shows that he sees no reason to separate them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What comes out of it?' – what is the practical difference?

phrases.english: He said to him:
What practical difference does it make?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Counter-question in response to step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why it would matter whether the ruling was said about חרוסת or about mustard.

steps.title: The difference comes from רב כהנא's view
steps.stepSummary: The questioner explains that according to רב כהנא, the dispute is only about mustard. With חרוסת, everyone agrees it must be burned immediately.
steps.simpleTranslation: It matters for the view of רב כהנא. רב כהנא said: The dispute is about flour put into mustard. But if flour is put into חרוסת, everyone agrees it must be burned immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains why he asked. רב כהנא holds that the חכמים are lenient only with mustard, not with חרוסת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב כהנא, flour in חרוסת becomes חמץ so quickly that even the חכמים agree it must be burned right away. So if רב הונא meant 'the הלכה follows the חכמים' even for חרוסת, he would be disagreeing with רב כהנא. The question is really asking: do you agree with רב כהנא or not?

keyTerms.meaning: The dispute (here, between רבי מאיר and the חכמים)
Everyone agrees
It must be burned immediately

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not saying that חרוסת is a different kind of food. He is saying that in the חרוסת case, even the lenient חכמים agree to burn it, because it becomes חמץ so fast.

phrases.english: It matters for the view of Rav Kahana.
For Rav Kahana said:
The dispute is about flour put into mustard,
but if put into charoset —
everyone agrees it must be burned immediately.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the counter-question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference depends on רב כהנא. He limits the dispute to mustard and holds that flour in חרוסת must be burned according to everyone.

steps.title: רב הונא does not hold like רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says, 'I did not hear this.' The גמרא explains that this means he does not agree with רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I did not hear it – meaning, I do not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא rejects רב כהנא's distinction. For him, the חכמים are lenient with חרוסת too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא clarifies that 'I did not hear it' is not a confession of ignorance. It is a polite way of saying he disagrees. So his ruling 'the הלכה follows the חכמים' covers both mustard and חרוסת.

keyTerms.meaning: I did not hear it
That is to say
I do not hold that way (I disagree)

steps.confusionAlert: 'לא שמיע לי' here does not mean he simply had not heard of רב כהנא's teaching. The גמרא itself explains that it means 'I don't agree.'

phrases.english: He said to him: I did not hear it,
that is to say, I do not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא שְׁמִיעַ לִי, כְּלוֹמַר לָא סְבִירָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רב הונא's position on the issue raised in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא disagrees with רב כהנא. He holds that the חכמים are lenient even with חרוסת.

steps.title: רב אשי sides with רב כהנא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי states that רב כהנא's view is the more reasonable one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: It is reasonable to follow רב כהנא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his opinion that רב כהנא is correct. This sets up the next step, where he brings his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי takes the opposite side from רב הונא. He supports the distinction that flour in חרוסת must be burned according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with him
It is reasonable / it makes sense

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
It is reasonable to follow Rav Kahana,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposes רב הונא's position in step 4 by siding with רב כהנא from step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא's view is the more reasonable one: flour in חרוסת must be burned according to everyone.

steps.title: Proof from שמואל: vinegar causes leavening
steps.stepSummary: שמואל ruled against רבי יוסי, who held that vinegar shrinks grain and stops it from leavening. This implies that vinegar actually makes grain leaven. Since חרוסת contains vinegar, it becomes חמץ quickly.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is clear from what שמואל said: The הלכה is not like רבי יוסי. Doesn't this mean that vinegar does not shrink the grain, but in fact makes it leaven?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי proves his point using שמואל's ruling against רבי יוסי. רבי יוסי held that vinegar prevents leavening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי allowed soaking grain in vinegar because he held that vinegar 'shrinks' the grain and stops it from leavening. שמואל rejects רבי יוסי, and רב אשי reads that rejection to mean that vinegar actually speeds up leavening. חרוסת is made with vinegar, so flour put into it becomes חמץ fast, which is exactly why רב כהנא said everyone agrees it must be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה does not follow (this opinion)
'Isn't it that...?' – introduces an inference
Shrinking / contracting (which prevents leavening)
It actually causes leavening

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא holds that the חכמים are lenient even with flour in חרוסת. רב כהנא, supported by רב אשי, says that with חרוסת everyone agrees it must be burned. רב אשי's proof: שמואל rejected רבי יוסי's claim that vinegar prevents leavening, which implies that vinegar actually causes it, and חרוסת contains vinegar.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why חרוסת is treated more strictly than mustard. Its vinegar makes flour turn into חמץ quickly.

phrases.english: From the fact that Shmuel said:
The halakha is not in accordance with Rabbi Yosei.
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי held that vinegar shrinks grain and prevents leavening.

phrases.english: Isn't it that this means:
it is shrinking that vinegar does not do,
but rather it actually causes it to leaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי. מַאי לָאו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the proof for רב אשי's statement in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's view that flour in חרוסת becomes חמץ quickly, so everyone agrees it must be burned immediately.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמואל's ruling that the הלכה does not follow רבי יוסי (who held that vinegar prevents leavening). This implies that vinegar actually causes leavening.

steps.title: Perhaps vinegar does nothing at all to grain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from שמואל. Perhaps שמואל held that vinegar neither shrinks the grain nor makes it leaven.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Perhaps vinegar does not shrink the grain, and it also does not make it leaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from Step 6. It shows that שמואל's ruling does not have to mean that vinegar causes leavening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof assumed only two options: if vinegar does not shrink the grain, it must make it leaven. The גמרא offers a third option: vinegar has no effect either way. So we cannot use שמואל to prove that חרוסת quickly becomes חמץ, and רב אשי's support is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; signals another way to read the source
Actually causes shrinking (makes the grain tighten)
Actually causes leavening

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל disagreeing with רבי יוסי does not automatically mean he holds the opposite. He may simply hold that vinegar has no effect at all.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from שמואל fails because there is a middle option: vinegar neither shrinks nor leavens.

phrases.english: No, perhaps
phrases.notes: This is the usual way the גמרא pushes back on a suggestion.

phrases.english: it does not cause shrinking at all,
and it does not cause leavening either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from שמואל, not רב אשי's view itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed vinegar must either shrink or leaven grain. It ignored the option that vinegar does neither.

steps.title: The ברייתא asks about boiling the פסח in other liquids
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that one may not boil the פסח. A ברייתא notes that the פסוק says ״בַּמָּיִם״ and asks where we learn that other liquids are also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says one may not boil the פסח. The רבנן taught: the פסוק says "in water." That only tells me about water. How do I know other liquids are forbidden too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה. It quotes a ברייתא that asks a question, and the next steps will give the answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק (שמות יב:ט) forbids eating the פסח ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל בַּמָּיִם״, boiled in water. Read literally, it mentions only water. So the ברייתא needs a source that boiling in wine, oil, or other liquids is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not boil (the opening words quoted from the משנה)
I only know; the plain words cover only this case
Other liquids
From where do we know?

phrases.english: "One may not boil," etc.
phrases.notes: Quotes the משנה to open the new discussion

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: "In water"
I only know about water;
how do I know about other liquids?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״בְּמַיִם״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא בְּמַיִם, שְׁאָר מַשְׁקִין מִנַּיִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, unrelated to the חרוסת discussion
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that boiling the פסח in liquids other than water is also forbidden

steps.title: First answer: a קל וחומר from water
steps.stepSummary: Water does not weaken the meat's taste, yet it is forbidden. Other liquids do weaken the taste, so they are surely forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can learn it with a קל וחומר. Water does not weaken the taste of the meat, and still boiling in it is forbidden. Other liquids do weaken the taste, so boiling in them is certainly forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question with a קל וחומר, a logical "how much more so" argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח must keep the taste of meat roasted over fire. Water changes the meat's taste less than other liquids do, and the Torah still forbids it. So liquids that change the taste even more must be forbidden as well.

keyTerms.meaning: A "how much more so" argument, from a lighter case to a stronger one
Weaken or change the taste (of the meat)
Is it not all the more so!

phrases.english: You said: it is a קל וחומר:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה מַיִם שֶׁאֵין מְפִיגִין טַעְמָן — אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: If water, which does not weaken the taste, is forbidden,
then other liquids, which do weaken the taste,
are they not all the more so forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Other liquids are forbidden through a קל וחומר: they affect the meat's taste more than water does.

steps.title: רבי learns it from the words ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״
steps.stepSummary: רבי asks the same question but finds a source in the פסוק itself. The doubled phrase ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ means boiling in any way is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: "In water" only tells me about water. How do I know about other liquids? The פסוק says "or boiled, boiled," meaning in any way at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי gives a second, different source for the same rule. He uses the wording of the פסוק instead of a logical argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have said just ״בָּשֵׁל״, boiled. The doubled form ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ broadens the ban to any kind of boiling, in any liquid. Both views agree that other liquids are forbidden. As the next steps show, the different sources do lead to a practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; introduces a source from the verse
"Or boiled, boiled"; the doubled wording in the פסוק
In any case; in any way at all

steps.whatToRemember: Boiling the קרבן פסח is forbidden in any liquid. The תנא קמא learns this from a קל וחומר, and רבי learns it from the doubled words ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי and the תנא קמא agree that all liquids are forbidden. However, their different sources do produce a practical difference, צלי קדר, which the גמרא explains in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: "In water"
I only know about water;
how do I know about other liquids?
The verse teaches: "or boiled, boiled"
meaning in any way at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: ״בְּמַיִם״ — אֵין לִי אֶלָּא מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different source, from the פסוק, for the same answer as Step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The doubled wording ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ includes boiling in every liquid.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: תנאים agree on the main law but use different sources, logic (קל וחומר) or the wording of the פסוק. The גמרא then looks for a case where the different sources lead to different results.

steps.title: What is the practical difference between the two sources?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי's source and the רבנן's source lead to different results.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: We just saw two different sources for forbidding the boiling of the פסח. Now the גמרא asks whether the two sources ever lead to a different result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן learned their rule from a קל וחומר based on ״בַּמָּיִם״. רבי learned it from the doubled words ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״. When two sources are given, the גמרא wants to know if they ever lead to different laws.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference between them? (asks for a practical difference)

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?
phrases.notes: Between רבי's source and the רבנן's source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the two sources given in steps 9-10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where רבי and the רבנן would rule differently.

steps.title: The difference is meat cooked in a pot in its own juices
steps.stepSummary: The two sources differ about צלי קדר, meat cooked in a pot with no liquid added.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is 'pot-roasting', meat cooked in a pot in its own juices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two views differ about צלי קדר. That is meat cooked in a pot with no water or other liquid added.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's source is about water and other liquids, so for them it only counts as boiling when liquid is added. רבי reads ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ as 'any kind of boiling'. So for him, cooking in the meat's own juices is also forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Pot-roast: meat cooked in a pot in its own juices, with no liquid added
There is a difference between them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not be misled by the word צלי ('roast'). It is not real fire-roasting, so according to רבי it counts as forbidden boiling.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule: a פסח must be roasted directly by fire, not cooked in a pot.

phrases.english: The difference between them is pot-roasting.
phrases.notes: Meat cooked in a pot in its own juices. Forbidden for רבי, allowed by the רבנן's source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: צלי קדר is forbidden for רבי ('any boiling') and not forbidden by the רבנן's source (which needs a liquid).

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from the doubled phrase?
steps.stepSummary: Since the רבנן do not use ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ the way רבי does, the גמרא asks what they learn from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this phrase ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the extra words ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״, since they did not use them for 'any kind of boiling'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes no words in the תורה are extra. If the רבנן do not learn רבי's lesson from the doubled phrase, they must learn some other lesson from it.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (what do they learn from this verse?)
'Boiled, cooked': the doubled phrase in the פסוק

phrases.english: And the Rabbis, this phrase 'boiled, cooked'
phrases.notes: The extra wording that רבי used as his source.

phrases.english: what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל מַאי עָבְדִי לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the views have been shown to differ, asks how the רבנן explain the phrase רבי relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״.

steps.title: The phrase teaches liability for boiling before or after roasting
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן use the phrase for a ברייתא. One who boiled and then roasted the פסח, or roasted and then boiled it, is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what was taught in a ברייתא: If he boiled it and then roasted it, or roasted it and then boiled it, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the doubled phrase for another law. Boiling the פסח makes one liable even if it was also roasted, whichever came first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think roasting at any point is enough to fix things. The extra words teach that boiling at any stage, before or after roasting, makes the person liable.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for (another teaching)
He roasted it
He boiled it
Liable (here, to מלקות)

phrases.english: It is needed for that which was taught in a baraita:
if he boiled it and afterward roasted it,
or he roasted it and afterward boiled it —
he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by giving the רבנן's use of the phrase.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ teaches liability for boiling either before or after roasting.

steps.title: Why is one liable for boiling meat that was already roasted?
steps.stepSummary: Boiling first and then roasting makes sense as liable. But if the meat was roasted first, it is already fire-roasted, so why is one liable?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that if he boiled it and then roasted it he is liable, because he boiled it. But if he roasted it and then boiled it, it is already fire-roasted. Why is he liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the second case of the ברייתא. Once meat is roasted, it seems it should keep its 'roasted' status, so boiling afterward should not matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case the boiling happened while the meat was still raw, so it is clearly a forbidden act. In the second case the meat already became צלי אש, the required 'fire-roasted' state. Why should boiling it afterward change that?

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense that (accepts one case before challenging another)
Fire-roasted, the way the תורה requires the פסח
Why?

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא בִּשְּׁלוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ צְלָאוֹ חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: Granted, if he boiled it and afterward roasted it he is liable,
since he boiled it.
But if he roasted it and afterward boiled it,
it is fire-roasted, so why is he liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא בִּשְּׁלוֹ וְאַחַר כָּךְ צְלָאוֹ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second case of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that one who roasted and then boiled is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once meat is fire-roasted it seems to have its required status, so boiling it afterward should not make one liable.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי. He holds that boiling after roasting cancels the roasted status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Whose view is this? It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the challenge by saying which תנא the ברייתא follows. It follows רבי יוסי, and the next step proves what רבי יוסי holds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא does not argue with the challenge's logic in general. He says there is a תנא who holds that later boiling cancels earlier roasting. So the meat is now treated as boiled, not roasted.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא הָא מַנִּי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Roasted meat stays 'roasted' even if boiled afterward.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי יוסי, boiling after roasting cancels the roasted status, so the person is liable.

steps.title: Proof from רבי יוסי's view on a boiled מצה wafer
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יוסי says a boiled wafer is not valid מצה, even if it has not dissolved. Boiling cancels its 'baked' status.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: One fulfills his obligation with a soaked wafer, and with a boiled wafer that has not dissolved. These are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יוסי says: One fulfills his obligation with a soaked wafer, but not with a boiled one, even if it has not dissolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove what רבי יוסי holds. For him, a baked מצה that is later boiled no longer counts as 'baked bread'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says baking status stays as long as the wafer has not dissolved. רבי יוסי says boiling cancels it, so the wafer is now 'boiled', not 'baked'. Apply this to the פסח: boiling after roasting cancels the meat's roasted status, so the person is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: One fulfills his obligation (here, the מצוה of eating מצה)
A thin מצה wafer
Soaked
Dissolved, fell apart

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוסי, cooking later cancels an earlier 'baked' or 'roasted' status. That is why roasting and then boiling the פסח still makes one liable.
steps.confusionAlert: Soaking is not the same as boiling. Even רבי יוסי allows a soaked wafer. Only boiling cancels its 'baked' status.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:
One fulfills his obligation with a soaked wafer
and with a boiled one that has not dissolved,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:
One fulfills his obligation with a soaked wafer,
but not with a boiled one,
even if it has not dissolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא's claim about רבי יוסי's view.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי holds boiling cancels an earlier baked or roasted status.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי יוסי rules that a boiled wafer is not valid מצה even if it has not dissolved.

steps.title: עולא: Even רבי מאיר agrees, because the verse says boiled in any way
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives a second answer to the קשיא of step 15. Even רבי מאיר, who does not say boiling cancels the baked status of מצה, would agree that a פסח roasted and then boiled is forbidden. The reason is that the פסוק ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ forbids boiling in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: You can even say the ברייתא follows רבי מאיר. Here it is different, because the verse says ״וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״, meaning boiled in any way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different answer from עולא to the earlier question: why is someone liable if he roasted the פסח first and then boiled it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא had to say the ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, who holds that boiling cancels the earlier 'baked' or 'roasted' status. עולא says this is not needed. רבי מאיר may hold that a boiled wafer is still valid מצה, but with the פסח the Torah doubled the word (״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״). That doubling teaches that any boiling is forbidden, even boiling after roasting.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Here it is different.' Used to show that one case has its own special rule
'In any case.' Here: any kind of boiling, no matter what happened before it

steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not arguing about מצה. He agrees that by רבי מאיר boiling does not cancel 'baked' status in general. He is only saying the פסח has a special verse that forbids boiling in every situation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key method of the גמרא: a ruling that seems to depend on a מחלוקת can sometimes be explained according to both sides, using an extra word in the פסוק.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
You can even say it follows Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: רבי מאיר holds that a boiled wafer is still valid מצה, so boiling does not cancel 'baked' status.

phrases.english: it is different here, because the verse says:
'nor boiled in any way': in any case.
phrases.notes: The doubled word teaches that boiling is forbidden even after roasting.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רב כהנא's answer (step 16), so the ברייתא no longer has to depend on רבי יוסי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special verse (גזירת הכתוב) that sets the פסח apart from מצה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the ברייתא could only follow רבי יוסי, who holds that boiling cancels the roasted status.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבי מאיר agrees, because ״בָּשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ forbids boiling the פסח in any case, even after roasting.

steps.title: A ברייתא: roasting the פסח fully is not forbidden
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who roasts the פסח 'fully' is not liable. The פסוק only forbids meat that is partially roasted (נא) or boiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One might think that if he roasted it fully, he is liable. So the verse says: 'Do not eat of it partially roasted or boiled in water.' I told you partially roasted and boiled are forbidden, but not something roasted fully.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that uses the same פסוק to show what is NOT included in the prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא considers that since 'under-roasted' (נא) is forbidden, maybe 'over-roasted' is forbidden too. The פסוק lists only two forbidden things, נא and boiled. So roasting 'all the way' is not part of the לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I might have thought.' Opens a possible but wrong idea
'The verse teaches.' Brings the פסוק that corrects the wrong idea
Partially roasted, not cooked enough
'All its need': fully, all the way

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל צְלָאוֹ כׇּל צוֹרְכּוֹ יְהֵא חַיָּיב —
phrases.english: I might think that if he roasted it fully, he is liable —
therefore the verse says:
'Do not eat of it partially roasted,
nor boiled in any way in water.'
I told you partially roasted and boiled are forbidden,
but not when he roasted it fully.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל צְלָאוֹ כׇּל צוֹרְכּוֹ יְהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the roasted-then-boiled case to a new question about the same פסוק: what counts as outside the prohibition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roasting the פסח fully is not included in the לאו of נא and boiled.

steps.title: What case is the baraita talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means. Roasting fully is exactly how the פסח is supposed to be eaten, so why would anyone think it is forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step by asking what kind of 'full roasting' the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normal full roasting is the מצוה itself, so no one would think it is forbidden. The ברייתא must be talking about something more extreme. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is it like?' A request to define the exact case

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact case in the ברייתא of step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'roasted it fully' mean, if normal roasting is obviously allowed?

steps.title: רב אשי: He charred it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the ברייתא means the meat was roasted so much that it became charred. Even so, the לאו of נא and boiled does not apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: The case is where he made it charred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question: 'fully roasted' means roasted until it is burnt or charred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think over-roasting to the point of charring is forbidden, just as under-roasting is. The ברייתא, as רב אשי explains it, teaches that charring does not break this לאו. The פסוק only forbids under-roasted or boiled meat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'That he made it into'
Charred, burnt

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Where he made it charred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא is talking about meat roasted so much that it was charred. Even that is not included in the לאו.

steps.title: A ברייתא: eating the פסח raw is not included in this prohibition
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא teaches that one who eats a כזית of the פסח raw is not liable under this לאו. The פסוק only names partially roasted and boiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One might think that if he ate a כזית raw, he is liable. So the verse says: 'Do not eat of it partially roasted or boiled.' I told you partially roasted and boiled are forbidden, but not raw.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that limits the same פסוק. Raw meat is not part of this prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think raw meat is even worse than partially roasted meat, so it should certainly be forbidden. The ברייתא reads the פסוק strictly: it lists only נא and boiled. So eating raw does not make one liable for this לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized amount, the minimum amount of eating that makes one liable
Raw, completely uncooked

steps.confusionAlert: This ברייתא only says that eating raw does not break the לאו of נא and boiled. It does not say raw is a proper way to eat the פסח, which must be eaten roasted.
steps.whatToRemember: The לאו of ״אַל תֹּאכְלוּ מִמֶּנּוּ נָא וּבָשֵׁל מְבֻשָּׁל״ covers only two things: under-roasted and boiled meat. Boiling counts even after roasting (עולא). Charred meat and raw meat are not included in this לאו.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אָכַל כְּזַיִת חַי יְהֵא חַיָּיב —
phrases.english: I might think that if he ate an olive-bulk raw, he is liable —
therefore the verse says:
'Do not eat of it partially roasted, nor boiled in any way.'

phrases.aramaic: נָא וּבָשֵׁל אָמַרְתִּי לְךָ, וְלֹא חַי.
phrases.english: I told you partially roasted and boiled are forbidden, but not raw.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל אָכַל כְּזַיִת חַי יְהֵא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ברייתא to step 19. That one excluded over-roasting, and this one excludes eating raw.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating the פסח raw is not included in the לאו of נא and boiled.

steps.title: Raw meat is still forbidden because of 'roasted with fire'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. One might think eating the פסח raw is allowed, so the פסוק ״כִּי אִם צְלִי אֵשׁ״ teaches that it must be roasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think it is permitted to eat it raw. Therefore the פסוק says: 'But roasted with fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 22 finishes its thought. Raw meat is not covered by the לאו of נא and boiled, but that does not make it permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 22 said a person who eats the פסח raw is not liable under the לאו. Someone could wrongly conclude that raw is fine. The words ״כִּי אִם צְלִי אֵשׁ״ add a positive command (עשה): the פסח must be roasted, so raw meat is still not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think it is permitted
Therefore the פסוק teaches
Roasted with fire

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not liable' (פטור) is not the same as 'permitted' (מותר). Eating the פסח raw breaks no לאו, but it still goes against the command to roast it.

phrases.english: One might think it is permitted —
the verse states: 'But roasted with fire.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating the פסח raw is forbidden through the positive command of צלי אש, even though no לאו applies.

steps.title: What counts as partially roasted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a definition of the word נא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly is נא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of cooking the פסוק means by נא. This sets up רב's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתות have contrasted raw meat, charred meat, and נא. To know when the לאו applies, we need to know exactly where נא falls between raw and fully roasted.

keyTerms.meaning: What are the circumstances? What does it look like?
Partially roasted meat

phrases.english: What are the circumstances of na (partially roasted)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a term used in the ברייתות.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A definition of the term נא.

steps.title: רב defines it as half-roasted, using a Persian word
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that נא is what the Persians call אברנים, meaning half-roasted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: It is what the Persians call אברנים, meaning half-roasted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers the question by pointing to a Persian word for meat that is only half-roasted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נא is neither raw nor fully roasted. It is meat that has started roasting but is still only partly cooked. This places נא between raw (step 22) and charred (step 21).

keyTerms.meaning: Persians
Half-roasted (a Persian word)

phrases.english: Rav said:
As the Persians say: avarnim (half-roasted).
phrases.notes: The גמרא uses a familiar foreign word to explain a word from the תורה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.

steps.title: Cooking in hot springs: exempt on שבת, liable for the פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא rules that cooking in the hot springs of טבריא on שבת carries no liability, but boiling a פסח in them makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: One who cooks in the hot springs of טבריא on שבת is exempt. A פסח that was boiled in the hot springs of טבריא makes one liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. רב חסדא gives two rulings about the same hot springs that seem to point in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, cooking in natural hot springs is not counted as forbidden cooking. Yet for the פסח, רב חסדא says boiling it in the same springs makes one liable. This contrast sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The natural hot springs of טבריא
Exempt, not liable
Liable

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
One who cooks in the hot springs of Tiberias on Shabbat is exempt.
A Pesach offering that one boiled in the hot springs of Tiberias: he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא הַמְבַשֵּׁל בְּחַמֵּי טְבֶרְיָא בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: boiling with heat that does not come from fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooking in hot springs on שבת carries no liability, but boiling a פסח in them makes one liable.

steps.title: Hot springs are not fire for the פסח either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two cases differ. On שבת, cooking must come from fire or something derived from fire, and hot springs are neither. The same should be true for the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is שבת different, that one is not liable? Because we need something derived from fire, and here there is none. But for the פסח too, hot springs are not derived from fire!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא. It first explains the שבת rule, then shows that the same reasoning should apply to the פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת, only heat from fire, or from something fire has heated (תולדות אש), counts as cooking. Hot springs are heated naturally, not by fire. Boiling the פסח in them should then also not count as boiling, so why does רב חסדא call it liable?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
Derivatives of fire, meaning something heated by fire
We require

phrases.english: What is different about Shabbat, that one is not liable?
Because we require a fire derivative, and there is none.

phrases.aramaic: פֶּסַח נָמֵי, לָאו תּוֹלְדוֹת אֵשׁ הוּא!
phrases.english: The Pesach too: it is not a fire derivative!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the contrast in רב חסדא's two rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling that one who boils a פסח in hot springs is liable.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hot springs are not derived from fire. If that keeps them from counting as cooking on שבת, it should also keep them from counting as boiling the פסח.

steps.title: רבא: liable for not roasting it with fire
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'liable' means the person broke the command of צלי אש, not the לאו against boiling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What does 'liable' mean in רב חסדא's teaching? That he broke the command of 'roasted with fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by reading the word 'liable' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that hot springs do not count as boiling, so the לאו against boiling does not apply. The person is still at fault, because the פסח was not roasted with fire as the פסוק commands. This matches the idea from step 23 that the עשה of צלי אש covers cases the לאו does not reach.

keyTerms.meaning: That he taught
He violated because of a certain command

steps.whatToRemember: Boiling the פסח in hot springs breaks no לאו against boiling, since hot springs are not fire. It still fails the positive command to roast the פסח with fire.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the meaning of 'liable' that he taught?
That he violated the command of 'roasted with fire.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of a term: 'liable' refers to the עשה, not the לאו.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Liable' was understood as breaking the לאו against boiling.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Liable' means breaking the עשה of צלי אש, since hot springs do not count as boiling.

steps.title: Another tradition reports רב חסדא's ruling with the explanation built in
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בריה דרב נתן teaches רב חסדא's statement explicitly. Cooking in the hot springs of טבריא on שבת is פטור. A פסח cooked in them makes one חייב, because he did not fulfill the command of צלי אש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חייא, the son of רב נתן, taught רב חסדא's statement with the explanation stated openly. רב חסדא said: One who cooks in the hot springs of טבריא on שבת is exempt. But if a פסח was cooked in the hot springs of טבריא, he is liable, because he broke the command of 'roasted with fire.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב חסדא's ruling. In this version, רב חסדא himself says the explanation that רבא suggested.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 28, רבא had to explain what 'חייב' meant: the person failed to fulfill צלי אש, and he did not break the לאו against boiling. Here רב חייא reports that רב חסדא actually said those words: 'שעבר משום צלי אש'. So the question from Step 27 never starts, because the hot springs still do not count as 'cooking' in the halachic sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly, openly stated
The natural hot springs of Tiberias
Exempt, no liability
Liable
Because he broke the command of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'חייב' as liability for בישול (cooking). Hot springs are not cooking, for שבת or for the פסח. The only problem is that the meat was not roasted by fire, as צלי אש requires.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבא's answer was not just a way to escape the question. It was the original wording of רב חסדא's ruling in another tradition.

phrases.english: Rav Chiyya, son of Rav Natan,

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא בְּהֶדְיָא.
phrases.english: teaches this statement of Rav Chisda explicitly.
Rav Chisda said:
One who cooks in the hot springs of Tiberias on Shabbat is exempt,
and a Paschal lamb that one cooked in the hot springs of Tiberias makes him liable,
phrases.notes: Liable for not fulfilling the positive command. It is not the לאו of boiling.

phrases.english: because he violated the command of 'roasted with fire.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִיָּיא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן מַתְנֵי לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַב חִסְדָּא בְּהֶדְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms רבא's answer from Step 28 by bringing a tradition in which רב חסדא himself states that explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cooking in the hot springs of טבריא is not cooking for שבת. A פסח prepared that way makes one liable only because the command of צלי אש was not fulfilled.

steps.title: רבא begins a new ruling about eating the פסח half-roasted
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a new statement about someone who eats the פסח as נא (half-roasted). The ruling itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he ate it half-roasted...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new statement of רבא about eating the פסח half-roasted. This line only sets up the case. The ruling comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא defined נא as אברנים, meaning half-roasted (Steps 24–25). Now רבא begins to discuss the punishment for actually eating it in that state. The case is presented here, and the legal outcome has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: He ate it (the פסח)
Half-roasted, not fully cooked (the Torah's 'אל תאכלו ממנו נא')

phrases.english: Rava said:
If one ate it partially roasted —
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the hot springs discussion to a new statement about the prohibition of eating the פסח as נא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The case is set up (eating the פסח half-roasted). The ruling follows on the next amud.
